ECE 6390 / Waves and fields

E, H & energy

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows how perpendicular electric and magnetic fields carry energy along a propagation direction.

For a lossless uniform plane wave propagating along +x, one possible orientation is E along y and H along z. The fields are in phase and satisfy E/H = η = √(μ/ε), with η in ohms.

Instantaneous energy flux is S = E × H in W/m². Both fields reverse during half of the cycle, leaving their cross product directed along the same propagation direction.

For peak electric amplitude E₀, the time-average flux is E₀²/(2η). With RMS amplitude, the factor 1/2 is already contained in the amplitude conversion.

Example

A 10 V/m peak field in a medium with η = 377 Ω carries approximately 0.133 W/m² of average power flux.

    Practice

    1. At the same impedance, what happens to magnetic amplitude and average power flux if electric amplitude doubles?

    Use H₀ = E₀/η and ⟨S⟩ = E₀²/(2η).

    Magnetic amplitude doubles, while average power flux quadruples.
